content.title: About
content.content: A muffin is a small sweet quick bread, typically made from flour, eggs, sugar, butter, and leavening agents. This version includes pieces of fresh fruit (such as blueberries or kiwi), giving it a fragrant and nutritious boost.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Muffins originated in England in the 19th century as a fast way to use leftover batter.
There are countless fillings: berries, apples, bananas, citrus, and even vegetables.
Fruit muffins are often served with tea or coffee as a light snack.
Muffin batter is usually thicker than cake batter, giving the baked good its characteristic dense crumb.
Homemade muffins can be made gluten‑free by substituting wheat flour with rice or almond flour.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The fruit adds vitamin C, vitamin A, and folate, which support immune function.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fruit pieces and whole‑grain flour increase dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Energy providing
items.content: A balance of carbohydrates and modest fat content supplies sustained energy.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Berries such as blueberries contain anthocyanins that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Heart‑friendly fats
items.content: Healthy fats from butter or plant oils contribute to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to wheat, eggs, or specific fruits.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet muffins can contribute to weight gain if eaten in excess.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of butter and sugar, muffins are relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Muffins can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature. They are convenient for on‑the‑go snacking, pairing with tea, coffee, or as part of breakfast with yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer freshness keep them in the refrigerator (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months).
